title: Module 12 · PICU and Pediatric Emergencies
intro: The adult ceiling, PALS doses, adenosine and atropine, status epilepticus with ESETT, pediatric DKA and cerebral edema, RSI, withdrawal weans, fluids and dosing anchors, and poisonings.

cases.title: The adult ceiling
cases.stem: A 15 year old, 82 kg. Order: acetaminophen 15 mg/kg PO every 6 hours = 1,230 mg.

steps.q: What is wrong?

options.t: Never above the adult dose: cap 1,000 mg
Fine: 15 mg/kg applies at any weight
options.why: Weight based doses are capped at the adult dose.
Not the fix; use the adult cap.

options.t: Cap at 650 mg, the pediatric maximum
options.why: 650 mg is a common adult tablet dose, not the cap.

steps.q: Which other pediatric checks run on every order?

options.t: Measured weight in kg; actual vs ideal per drug
Standard concentration and a measurable volume
Weight in pounds as reported by the parent
Age in years alone to pick the dose

cases.pearl: **mg/kg, but never above the adult dose.**

sources.t: St. Mary's pediatric code sheet, drip library, DKA and sedation wean protocols (verify locally)

cases.title: Pediatric arrest
cases.stem: A 20 kg child in asystole. IO in place.

steps.q: Epinephrine dose?

options.why: The endotracheal dose; IV/IO is 0.01 mg/kg.
Right dose but 10x volume with the 1 mg/mL product.

steps.q: Rhythm changes to VF, refractory to shocks. Amiodarone?

options.t: 15 mg/kg = 300 mg as a single dose
options.why: 15 mg/kg is the total, not one dose.

cases.pearl: **PALS epi 0.01 mg/kg (0.1 mL/kg of 0.1 mg/mL). Amio 5 mg/kg.**

sources.t: AHA/AAP 2025 Pediatric Advanced Life Support (AHA CPR and ECC 2025, Part 8)
St. Mary's pediatric code sheet, drip library, DKA and sedation wean protocols (verify locally)

workup.calc: 20 kg: epinephrine 0.01 x 20 = 0.2 mg = **2 mL** of 0.1 mg/mL; amiodarone 5 x 20 = **100 mg**.

cases.title: Pediatric SVT and bradycardia
cases.stem: Two children: (A) 15 kg with SVT at 260, stable; (B) 10 kg with bradycardia from AV block.

steps.q: Adenosine for A?

options.why: Rapid push with flush; second dose max 12 mg.

steps.q: Atropine for B?

sources.t: AHA/AAP 2025 Pediatric Advanced Life Support (AHA CPR and ECC 2025, Part 8)

workup.calc: Adenosine 0.1 x 15 = 1.5 mg, then 0.2 x 15 = 3 mg. Atropine 0.02 x 10 = 0.2 mg.

cases.title: Status epilepticus in a child
cases.stem: A 25 kg child seizing for 8 minutes. No IV yet.

steps.q: First line without IV access?

options.t: Midazolam IM 5 mg (13 to 40 kg), once

options.why: Erratic IM absorption; rectal or IV used instead.

steps.q: IV placed, still seizing 5 minutes later. Lorazepam dose?

options.t: 0.1 mg/kg = 2.5 mg IV (max 4 mg), repeat once
4 mg IV, because that is the maximum dose
options.why: The cap, not the dose; 0.1 mg/kg here.

options.t: 0.05 mg/kg = 1.25 mg IV, repeat every 5 min

steps.q: Still seizing at 20 minutes. Second line options (ESETT: similar efficacy)?

options.t: Fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg (500 mg PE, max 1,500)

options.why: Avoid in mitochondrial or liver disease.
Move to second line after two doses.

cases.pearl: **SE: benzo (IM midaz 5 or 10 mg, or lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg), then levetiracetam, fosphenytoin or valproate.**

sources.t: Glauser T, et al. AES guideline: treatment of convulsive status epilepticus in children and adults. Epilepsy Curr 2016;16:48-61
Kapur J, et al. Randomized trial of three anticonvulsant medications for status epilepticus (ESETT). N Engl J Med 2019;381:2103-2113
St. Mary's pediatric code sheet, drip library, DKA and sedation wean protocols (verify locally)

workup.calc: 25 kg: lorazepam 0.1 x 25 = 2.5 mg; levetiracetam 60 x 25 = 1,500 mg; fosphenytoin 20 x 25 = 500 mg PE; valproate 40 x 25 = 1,000 mg.

cases.title: Pediatric DKA
cases.stem: A 30 kg child in DKA. K 4.2.

steps.q: Insulin plan?

options.t: 0.05 to 0.1 units/kg/h, no bolus, after hour 1
options.why: 1.5 to 3 units/h; start after the first hour of fluids (ISPAD).
Boluses raise cerebral edema risk in children.

options.t: 0.14 units/kg/h, no bolus, start at once
options.why: An adult no bolus rate; start after initial fluids.

options.t: 1 unit/kg/h IV, no bolus, after hour 1

steps.q: What emergency do you prepare for?

options.t: Cerebral edema: mannitol or 3% saline ready
options.why: Mannitol 0.5 to 1 g/kg or 3% 2.5 to 5 mL/kg.
Glucose is watched, but cerebral edema is the killer.

steps.q: How do pediatric and adult potassium cutoffs differ?

options.t: Children: start insulin at any potassium
options.why: Low K must be replaced first.

cases.pearl: **Peds DKA: no bolus, 0.05 to 0.1 units/kg/h, mannitol or 3% ready.**

sources.t: Glaser N, et al. ISPAD 2022 consensus guidelines: DKA and HHS. Pediatr Diabetes 2022;23:835-856
St. Mary's pediatric code sheet, drip library, DKA and sedation wean protocols (verify locally)

workup.calc: 30 kg: insulin 0.05 to 0.1 units/kg/h = 1.5 to 3 units/h; mannitol 0.5 to 1 g/kg = 15 to 30 g; 3% saline 2.5 to 5 mL/kg = 75 to 150 mL.

cases.title: Iatrogenic withdrawal
cases.setting: PICU · day 9 of fentanyl and midazolam
cases.stem: A child extubated after 9 days of fentanyl and midazolam infusions is irritable, sweaty, with diarrhea and tremors.

steps.q: What is this?

options.why: Iatrogenic; expected after 5 or more days of infusions.
Pattern fits withdrawal; check the WAT 1 score.

steps.q: What is the pharmacist role?

options.t: Wean plan (methadone, lorazepam), taper by scores
Restart the fentanyl infusion at full rate

cases.pearl: **5+ days of drips: expect withdrawal. WAT-1 and a wean.**

cases.title: Everyday pediatric doses and fluids
cases.stem: A 20 kg child admitted for dehydration.

steps.q: Maintenance fluid rate by Holliday Segar (4/2/1)?

options.t: 60 mL/h: 40 for first 10 kg + 20 for next 10

options.why: 4 mL/kg/h applies to the first 10 kg only.

options.t: 50 mL/h: 40 for first 10 kg + 10 for next 10

steps.q: Which fluid does AAP 2018 recommend for most hospitalized children?

options.t: Isotonic fluid with potassium and dextrose

steps.q: Acetaminophen and ibuprofen doses for 20 kg?

options.t: APAP 300 mg q6h; ibuprofen 200 mg q6 to 8h
APAP 200 mg q6h; ibuprofen 300 mg q6 to 8h
APAP 600 mg q6h; ibuprofen 400 mg q6 to 8h
APAP 1,000 mg q6h; ibuprofen 600 mg q6h

cases.pearl: **4/2/1, isotonic fluids, APAP 15 mg/kg, ibuprofen 10 mg/kg.**

sources.t: Feld LG, et al. AAP clinical practice guideline: maintenance IV fluids in children. Pediatrics 2018;142:e20183083

workup.calc: 20 kg: 4/2/1 = 40 + 20 = **60 mL/h**; acetaminophen 300 mg; ibuprofen 200 mg.

cases.title: Pediatric poisonings
cases.stem: A toddler may have swallowed a grandparent's glipizide.

steps.q: Beyond dextrose, which antidote prevents repeated lows?

options.why: Raises glucose briefly; can provoke more insulin release.

steps.q: Who do you call for help?

cases.pearl: **Sulfonylurea in a child: dextrose + octreotide, admit, call Poison Control.**
